opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: Thanks for making time, Robert. I'm a researcher with the Work Futures Panel, an independent group that studies how people see changes at work, and nothing you tell me will be linked to your name.

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: Fine. I'll say up front I don't use these AI things. My grandson keeps telling me I should.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Picture this. AI stays a handy tool, like a better search engine. Hiring, pay and prices carry on the way they would have anyway. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say good for those who use it. We run on written procedures here, and they've kept the water safe for decades.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Means nothing for me. I've only got a couple of years left. If it stays a tool, the next manager can decide what to do with it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do in the first year? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Nothing new. Train my deputy, keep the logs tidy, start planning for retirement.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Calm. Same as any year.

S0.say: Good for those who use it. Our written procedures have kept the water safe for decades.
S0.think: Means nothing for me. The next manager can decide what to do with it.
S0.do: Trains his deputy, keeps the logs tidy and plans for retirement.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Now picture this. Very capable AI exists, but it spreads slowly, over ten years or more. Some tasks disappear, but few whole jobs do. Companies hire fewer beginners. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say slow is how a water plant should change. Every new thing gets tested before it touches what people drink.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd be retired before anything big happens. Fewer beginners worries me a little for the plant, since we already struggle to find certified operators.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do in the first year? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Make sure the written procedures are up to date for whoever comes after me. Keep the trainee operator post funded if I can.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Calm. A bit concerned for the plant after I go.

S1.say: Slow is how a water plant should change. Everything gets tested before it touches what people drink.
S1.think: I'll be retired first. Fewer beginners worries me for the plant, though.
S1.do: Updates the written procedures for his successor and fights to keep the trainee operator post funded.
S1.feel: Calm, a bit concerned for the plant.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Next one. Within 5 years, AI assistants that can act on their own handle most routine office work. There are layoffs and pay pressure in office jobs. Some new AI-related jobs appear, and politicians argue loudly about what to do. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say a water plant is not routine office work, and the public should be glad of that.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: They'd probably want an agent on our reports and compliance paperwork. Fine. The regulator will still want a human name on it. I'm not worried for me.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do in the first year? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Let the deputy try the new tools if head office wants it. Make sure every change goes through our procedures first.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Calm. Not my battle.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: You don't use AI yourself. How do you judge what it can and can't do?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I don't, really. I go by what I read and what my grandson tells me. That's why I want everything tested.

S2.say: A water plant is not routine office work, and the public should be glad of that.
S2.think: They'd put an agent on the paperwork. The regulator will still want a human name on it.
S2.do: Lets his deputy try the new tools and makes sure every change goes through the plant's procedures first.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Now a faster version. Within 2 to 3 years, AI matches skilled professionals at most thinking work. Lots of office and professional workers lose their jobs. Share and house prices boom. There's a political crisis over who should get the gains. Physical jobs are mostly untouched. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say we need to slow down and check what we're doing. Things that move this fast tend to break.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Our savings and the house go up, so I'd retire on time and be fine. What bothers me is a plant like mine run by software with fewer people watching. My grandchildren drink that water.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do in the first year? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Retire on schedule, maybe a little early. Before I go, put it in writing that the plant keeps a qualified operator on every shift.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Uneasy. For the town more than me.

S3.say: We need to slow down and check what we're doing. Things that move this fast tend to break.
S3.think: I'd be fine. What bothers me is software running the plant with fewer people watching.
S3.do: Plans to retire on time and puts in writing that a qualified operator stays on every shift.
S3.feel: Uneasy, for the town more than himself.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Last one. Everything in the previous picture happens, and on top of that, general-purpose robots arrive in warehouses, kitchens, building sites, farms and care homes within 3 to 5 years. Hands-on work is no longer a safe place to be. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say a robot shouldn't be the last line of defence for what comes out of the tap.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: For me, nothing changes. I'm out the door. For my grandchildren, I don't know what work they'll find, and that worries me more than anything about the plant.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do in the first year? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Retire. Spend more time with the grandchildren. Help my kids out a bit if their jobs get shaky.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Uneasy. For the grandkids, mostly.

S4.say: A robot shouldn't be the last line of defence for what comes out of the tap.
S4.think: Nothing changes for me. I worry what work my grandchildren will find.
S4.do: Retires, spends more time with the grandchildren and helps his kids if their jobs get shaky.
